title: Women victims of violences : PTSD treatment by traumatic memory reactivation under the influence of propranolol (VIOFEM)
official: Women victims of violences : PTSD treatment by traumatic memory reactivation under the influence of propranolol (VIOFEM)
summary: Main objective: To evaluate, in a group of women who are victims of violence and suffer from PTSD, the effect of treatment consisting of 6 sessions (1 per week) of traumatic memory reactivation under propranolol/PPNL (a single dose of propranolol administered prior to the traumatic memory reactivation) compared to the effect of treatment with 8 sessions (1 per week) of prolonged exposure psychotherapy (EP) on PTSD symptoms.

interventions.name: PROPRANOLOL ARROW 40 mg, comprimé pelliculé sécable

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Women aged from 18 to 75 years
2. Having been victim of severe violence (rape, sexual assault, physical assault)
3. Currently suffering from PTSD related to the traumatic event. The diagnosis of PTSD is made according to the DSM-5 criteria by a psychiatrist/psychologist using the CAPS-5, regardless of the traumatic event meeting criterion A of the DSM-5, with or without dissociative symptoms as described in the “With dissociative symptoms” section of the DSM-5, Immediate or delayed PTSD
4. heart rate ≥ 55 bpm
5. The subject must have signed the consent form.
6. The subject must be enrolled in a social security program.
7. The participant must be able to understand and read French.
8. The participant agrees to comply with the contraception requirements outlined in the protocol
9. CAPS-5 total score ≥ 33
Exclusion criteria:
1. Systolic blood pressure below 100 mm Hg.
2. Patients who have suffered a head injury within the past year or who have clinical symptoms and residual neurological sequelae
3. Wearing contact lenses
4. Hospitalized or treated for suicidal behavior within the past 3 months
5. Previous intolerance to a beta-blocker.
6. Women of childbearing age not using contraception
7. Pregnancy, breastfeeding
8. Current use of a beta-blocker, regardless of the formulation.
9. Known interactions with Propranolol (combination use not recommended and combinations to be used with caution) as indicated in the summary of product characteristics
10. Undergoing psychotherapy or pharmacological treatment with psychotropic agents such as antidepressants, neuroleptics, and/or mood stabilizers. However, these subjects may be included after a 2-week therapeutic abstinence period (6 weeks for treatment with fluoxetine).
11. Patients under judicial protection, under guardianship or curatorship, individuals under family authorization, or under a future protection order with representation regarding the person
12. USevere psychiatric disorders: Severe symptoms of other anxiety disorders, severe symptoms of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder, history of or current psychotic disorder, bipolar mood disorder, severe personality disorder, alcohol or other substance use disorder
13. Participants who are related to a person involved in the study at the investigator’s center, within the clinical research organization (CRO), or at the sponsor
14. Participation in another interventional research study, clinical trial, or clinical investigation within the 6 months preceding selection
15. “Yes” response to item 4 of the C-SSRS: active suicidal ideation with intent to act, without a specific plan, and/or “Yes” response to item 5 of the C-SSRS: active suicidal ideation with a specific plan and intent to act
16. Propanolol contrindications
17. Heart failure (compensated or decompensated)
18. Severe liver disease
19. Significant renal impairment
20. Myasthenia gravis
21. Personal or family history of psoriasis
